## Check in the original equation {#substitution}

We found $x=2$ for $5x-2(x-3)=x+10$. Substitute into the **original equation** so an expansion error cannot hide in the check.

:::::: {.example-pair}
::::: {.model}

<h3>Left-hand side</h3>

::: {.fragment}

$5(2)-2(2-3)$

:::
::: {.fragment}

$=10-2(-1)$

:::
::: {.fragment}

$=10+2=12$

:::
:::::
::::: {.paper}
::: {.fragment}

<h3>Right-hand side</h3>

$2+10=12$

:::
::: {.fragment}

Both sides equal $12$, so $x=2$ is a solution.

:::
:::::
::::::

::: {.fragment}

**On paper:** check your solution $x=15$ in $4(x-3)=2x+18$. Calculate each side separately before selecting Next.

:::
::: {.fragment}

$\text{LHS}=4(15-3)=48,\qquad \text{RHS}=2(15)+18=48.$

The two sides agree, so the solution is verified.

:::
